newsitem.title: BRAZIL: World Bank delegation visits Brazil's Santos port.
newsitem.headline: World Bank delegation visits Brazil's Santos port.

text.p: A delegation of World Bank technicians is visiting Brazil's key port of Santos to collect data and map out a program of investment in infrastructure and training, the port authority Codesp said.
The four technicians will also visit Rio de Janeiro port and their findings will be used to prepare a port sector restructuring and modernization project, Codesp said in a statement.
"This project will permit financial and technical support through investment and personnel training," Robert Mosse, one of the World Bank team, was quoted as saying.
Both the Santos and Rio de Janeiro container terminals are scheduled to be privatized this year under a wide-ranging program to modernize Brazil's ports.
The technicians, who are scheduled to remain at Santos until July 16, will be assisted by a team of specialists from the port in collecting data and information.
They will only announce the size and form of the investment plan after having returned to Washington, Codesp said.
"The World Bank financing will probably take the shape of a special credit line for whoever is leasing the terminal," a spokesman for the port said.
